pageCache.pageTitle: St Edward's Royal Free Ecumenical Middle School - The Role and Responsibilities of the Governing Body
pageCache.text:
The Role and Responsibilities of the Governing Body
St. Edward’s Royal Free is a joint Anglican-Catholic Voluntary-Aided school.
The Governing Body’s primary purpose is to approve the strategic direction of the school, working in partnership with the Headteacher, and under the guidance of the Oxford and Portsmouth Dioceses.
Through strategic leadership and accountability, the Governing Body promotes continuous school improvement to achieve high standards of education for all our pupils, set within the Ecumenical nature and Christian ethos of our school.
There are three core functions of the Governing Body:
Aligned to its improvement role, the Governing Body is there to be a ‘critical friend’ providing a balance between supporting and challenging the performance of both the Headteacher and the school.
Our Scheme of Delegation sets out what powers our Governing Body has given to the committees, the Headteacher or individual Governors.
The Headteacher is delegated total responsibility for the running of the school and all associated operational matters; governors are not involved in the day-to-day operation of the school.
Our Foundation Principles document details how we work together with both the Dioceses.
The Structure of the Governing Body
The Instrument of Government is the legal document that outlines the constitution of the Governing Body for our school and the term of office for each category of Governor.
At St. Edward’s Middle School we have a total of 14 Governors, supported by a Clerk:
For binding decisions to be made, a Full Governing Body meeting must be quorate.
Committees are designed to help the Governing Body manage the wide range of duties and responsibilities by spreading the workload and allowing issues to be examined in detail. Minutes of committee meetings are submitted to the Full Governing Body for consideration and approval of recommendations.
At St. Edward’s Middle School we have three committees:
Each committee has a Terms of Reference detailing its purpose, its powers and its operation; these are reviewed annually to ensure our statutory duties are met and that the committees are working in the best interests of the school and the Governing Body.
Individual Governors take on particular tasks and/or make decisions on behalf of the Governing Body, but only when specifically given this responsibility by the Governing Body.
At St. Edwards Middle School we have the following Link Governors:
The responsibilities of the Link Governors are detailed in individual Role Descriptions.
The Governing Body endeavours to conduct its business in accordance with the Nolan Principles of public life: selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, honesty and leadership.
There are different routes by which different types of Governors are appointed but once appointed all Governors have equal status. The role of a Governor is a voluntary one.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Edward's Royal Free Ecumenical Middle School - Chairs' Welcome
pageCache.text:
Chairs' Welcome
On behalf of the Governors at St Edward’s Royal Free, I would like to offer you a very warm welcome to our school.
St Edward’s Royal Free is unique in being both a middle school and a joint Anglican-Catholic Voluntary-Aided school. It has been on its present site for 30 years but has existed for well over 300 years in various locations around Windsor.
In keeping with the Ecumenical nature and Christian ethos of St Edward’s, our mission is to provide a caring, happy and inclusive school with God at its centre, a place where the Christian values of respect and tolerance for each other flourish.
The governors, staff, pupils, and parents/carers work together to provide a rich and exciting learning environment for everyone; our core values of service, excellence, respect and faith underpin everything that we do.
As a middle school we are able to provide our primary pupils with expert teaching across a wide range of subjects. Our broad and balanced curriculum, and the array of extracurricular activities on offer enables each pupil to fulfil their academic potential whilst supporting their spiritual, and social and emotional development.
St Edward’s Royal Free is a wonderful school, and all of us who serve on the Governing Body are immensely proud of the achievements of the pupils and staff. We would also like to thank our parents/carers and the local community for their ongoing support in all that we do.
Further information about the Governing Body and the work that we do can be found in this section of the school website.
Louise Corfe and Kate Long
Co-Chairs of Governors

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Structure
“The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and planted in his field. Though it is the smallest of all seeds, when it grows it is the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree so that the birds come and perch in its branches” Matthew 13
Curriculum Booklet Year 5
Curriculum Booklet Year 6
Curriculum Booklet Year 7
Curriculum Booklet Year 8
statement of Intent
The curriculum is designed to support and challenge pupils to develop emotionally, academically and spiritually, centred around our Christian Ethos of growth and underpinned by our four values of Service, Excellence, Respect and Faith. It is designed to be engaging and ambitious and to meet the needs of all pupils, allowing them to develop their interests and aspirations. It cumulatively builds knowledge, understanding and skills and prepares them well for future learning and employment. The development of reading skills, mathematical skills and digital education are central to learning.
Implementation
Impact
Key Stage 2 Provision
The Key Stage 2 curriculum covers all children in Years 5 and 6 plus any extra-curricular activities and enrichment events. There are 25 lessons each week.
Classes in Year 5 are taught as 4 mixed-ability groups. The Literacy teacher will likely teach drama and PSHE as well as Humanities.
Classes in Year 6 are taught as 4 mixed-ability groups apart from Maths and English where five teachers are available to allow for smaller mixed ability classes.
Key Stage 3 Provision
The Key Stage 3 curriculum also comprises 25 lessons per week plus extra-curricular activities and enrichment events.
Religious Education / PSHE
In Year 7, 120 pupils are organised into 4 teaching groups. These are mixed ability groups for most subjects. Drama in Year 7 complements the English curriculum.
In Year 8, arrangements are the same as Year 7. Although instead of drama there is a lesson of options subjects (guided preferences): from MFL, Advanced Computer Science, Performing Arts, Humanities, Applied Sport and Exercise. This ‘Options’ lesson is strongly linked to our careers programme both through the process of choosing and through explicit links to careers related to the subject including visiting speakers.
At St. Edward’s Royal Free, we aim to meet all intentions laid out in the 2019 Ofsted framework documentation as well as all National curriculum requirements. We plan to complete a curriculum review and improvement over the next two years to ensure it is fit for purpose and in-line with new recommendations. This last year has also focused on a hybrid curriculum model with topics being moved and amended to suit remote learning needs.
Some years, we run a two week timetable model but the make up of lessons stays as above.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Edward's Royal Free Ecumenical Middle School - Breakfast & After School Club
pageCache.text:
breakfast and After School Club
BREAKFAST CLUB
Further to Mrs Adamson’s letter of 25th February concerning our successful application to be part of the Government’s Breakfast Club Early Adopter Scheme there will be changes to the booking of sessions for breakfast club via Scopay from 22nd April.
The existing booking system for the whole school will no longer be available after 4th April. From 4th April there will be a KS2 Free Breakfast Club for years 5 and 6 to book sessions and have access to a free breakfast from 22nd April. Please note that the free items will be limited to those approved by the government and pupils will still be able to buy additional items if they wish to and items will be charged at £1 each via the ParentPay account. There will be no charge for childcare.
Pupils in year 7 and 8 will need to book sessions from 22nd April via the KS3 Breakfast Club on Scopay. This is £5.00 per session for supervision with breakfast items continuing to be charged at £1 each via the ParentPay account.
Breakfast Club for both KS2 and KS3 will run from 7.30am – 8.15am in the school hall. Pupils should arrive for Breakfast Club via the pedestrian gate on Parsonage Lane and walk through the large grey gate outside reception to access the hall from the door that they usually enter for break and lunchtimes. The pedestrian gate on Parsonage Lane is open to enable pupils to enter promptly at 7.30am if needed. The main gates are also open until 8am and parents may drive onto the school site to drop their child at breakfast club if they are arriving before 8am.
Sessions for all year groups need to be booked in advance via Scopay but there will be no cost for KS2 sessions. Sessions are to be booked by 3pm the day before although as much notice as possible would be appreciated to ensure that we have the right number of staff in place to manage the number of pupils attending.
The guide on how to book a session can be found on Scopay: www.scopay.com/stedwardsroyalfree If you are unable to book a session please contact the office for assistance.
If you have booked a place but will not be using it (e.g your child is unwell) please contact us by 7.30am via breakfastclub@sterf.org.uk to let us know so that we do not have to contact you as we will be taking a register each morning for safeguarding purposes.
Pupils not attending breakfast club who arrive at school between 8.15am and 8.30am are also able to buy breakfast by entering the hall via the grey gates before they go to registration.
Please ensure that all payment accounts are topped up regularly and that they are in credit.
AFTER SCHOOL PROVISION
Our after-school provision is open daily in the school library from 3.00pm to 5.00pm. You can book a place for your child on a session-by-session basis and the charge for this is £10 per session.
Sessions must be booked in advance on Scopay.
Bookings can be made up to 11.30am on the day required.
Please note that funds need to be available on your account in order to book sessions (the system will prompt you to top up the account).
If you would like to book this facility, please see the guide below on how to book a session on Scopay. Places are limited and if you are unable to book a session it may be because there are no places available for that day.
Sessions can be amended/cancelled in advance and this will add a credit to your account for a future session to be booked. Unfortunately, if a session has been booked but is not attended then we will be unable to offer a refund.
If you book a place but will not be using it, please telephone the school office on 01753 867809 by 2.30pm to let us know, so that we do not phone home as we will be taking a register each day for safeguarding purposes.
Booking sessions on Scopay - a parent's guide
EMERGENCY CONTACT
If parents need to contact the staff supervising wraparound care outside of normal office hours, they can do so by ringing 07546 645448. Please note that this number is only for emergency wraparound care contact. All other communication should be via the school office.

"Young adults who recall four or more encounters with employers while at school are five times less likely to be NEET and earn, on average, 18% more than peers who recall no such activities." (Dr Anthony Mann, Director of Research and Policy, Education and Employers Task Force)
Careers education and guidance programmes play a major part in helping young people choose pathways that suit their interests, abilities and individual needs. A robust careers programme helps avoid disengagement, puts school learning into a wider and more relevant context, and helps raise aspirations.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Edward's Royal Free Ecumenical Middle School - Admissions Appeals
pageCache.text:
Admissions Appeals
When the local authority or school has informed a parent / carer of the decision to refuse their child a place at the school, the parent / carer has the right to appeal.
The office of the Schools Adjudicator (OSA) states that Parents do not have an entitlement to choose a place at a school in any particular Ofsted category, or for that matter, the school closest to their home, of a particular religious character or other specific characteristic. Parents express a preference for a school and if that school is oversubscribed, criteria are used to determine which children are offered places and which are not.
OSA judgements carry the force of law, so neither the local authorities nor schools are legally allowed to consider anything irrelevant to the oversubscription criteria when awarding school places. Details of our oversubscription criteria can be found in our admissions policy.
We would like to make parents aware that when an appeal is lodged there are considerable costs involved, which are borne by the school from our existing budget.
Appeals can be made online via the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead’s website or via email to democratic.services@rbwm.gov.uk.
